sonnet.problem: The card tells David's cover-up scheme (the king's gift sent after Uriah while he is trying to hide his sin with Bathsheba), but it carries a joke about the gift and the junk drawer.
sonnet.rule: A card that tells death, violence, abuse, serious sin or the body's private matters has no joke.

sonnet.problem: The card tells Uriah's oath of loyalty inside David's attempt to hide his adultery. The joke about Uriah turning down 'a free night in his own bed' (his wife) and the snooze button trivializes the moment and leans toward innuendo.
sonnet.rule: A card that tells death, violence, abuse, serious sin or the body's private matters has no joke.

sonnet.problem: The card says Joab 'expects' David to bring up Abimelech. The text only says David 'may ask' this 'if the king's anger flares'. The conditional is turned into an expectation.
'Without waiting for the king to ask' adds a detail the text doesn't give. The text never says David was about to ask or that the messenger skipped a question.
sonnet.rule: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

sonnet.problem: 'That anger Joab warned about never shows up' states as fact something the text leaves open. Joab only said David's anger might flare, and the text doesn't say whether it did.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
